item.title: Ehime Kamaboko and Seafood Products — Guide
item.description: Ehime’s long coastline and rich fishing grounds have made it a leading producer of kamaboko and other fish-paste (nerimono) products, especially around the southern port of Yawatahama. Kamaboko is a smooth, springy cake of steamed white fish paste, mild and delicate, often sliced and eaten as is, in soups or with a little wasabi and soy. Alongside it, local makers produce a whole family of related products — grilled kamaboko, tube-shaped chikuwa, deep-fried varieties and the robust jakoten — all showcasing the freshness of the local catch.

item.title: Odawara Kamaboko & Seafood Guide: What to Eat & Access
item.description: The castle town of Odawara, gateway to Hakone, is one of Japan’s great homes of kamaboko — the springy steamed fish cake refined here over centuries thanks to fresh Sagami Bay catch and clean mountain water. Beyond the famous pink-and-white loaves, Odawara serves up fresh fish, grilled age-kama fritters, and a lively port market. Visitors can tour kamaboko makers, taste the difference between artisan and everyday versions, and even make their own at hands-on workshops.
